examples.en: I take public transport to work.
How much does the ride to the airport cost?
This winter we're going to Kopaonik.
The winter was mild this year.
Grandma reads the Bible every evening.
That quote is from the Bible.
Add a little olive oil.
The oil in the car needs to be changed.

examples.sr: Ти си [ге̏није], то је савршено решење!
examples.en: You're a genius, that's the perfect solution!
Tesla was a true genius.
She was pushing the baby in a stroller.
Take a shopping cart.
He wanted to become famous.
She met a famous singer.
He works extra hours on weekends.
Are there any additional questions?
He dragged a heavy suitcase to the station.
Don't pull me by the sleeve.

tips: On shop doors «Вуци» (or «Вуците») means «Pull»; the opposite sign is «Гурај» (Push).

examples.en: He hasn't been in touch since he moved.
She has been happy since she met him.
What does this expression mean?
He had a strange expression on his face.
The state governor gave a speech.

examples.sr: [Гувѐрне̄р] Народне банке најавио је нове мере.
examples.en: The Governor of the National Bank announced new measures.
The lion is the king of the animals.
We saw lions at the zoo.
Drive safely!
Is it safe to swim here?
Killing animals for fun is forbidden.
Stop the killing!
The universe is infinite.

examples.sr: Земља је само мала тачка у [универзу̀му].
examples.en: The Earth is just a small dot in the universe.
I take that as a personal insult.
That wasn't an insult, just a joke.
There was a hard frost last night.

examples.sr: Деда [Мра̏з] доноси поклоне за Нову годину.
examples.en: Father Frost brings presents for New Year.

tips: Мраз is severe cold; Деда Мраз is Father Frost, the Slavic New Year gift-bringer.
«Мраз је» means it is freezing outside.

examples.sr: Нови посао је за мене велики [и̏зазо̄в].
examples.en: The new job is a big challenge for me.
Challenge accepted!
What are you hiding behind your back?
He's hiding something from us.
For homework, do exercise number three.
This exercise strengthens the back muscles.
Let's go for a walk along the river.
Every morning I take the dog for a walk.
Someone is knocking at the door.
He types fast on the computer.

tips: Also used for typing a message: «куцати поруку/смс» means to type a text message.

examples.en: He is a citizen of Serbia.
Citizens turned out in large numbers to vote.
He brought a sack of potatoes.
I slept in a sleeping bag.

tips: Another word for a sack is «џак» (colloquial): «џак кромпира». Do not confuse it with «ђак» (schoolchild).

examples.en: His parents don't let him go out.
Smoking is not allowed here.
An unknown number called me.
An unfamiliar man was standing at the door.
Can you swim?
The children are swimming in the lake.
I work out at the gym three times a week.
You need to practice the piano more.
I drink two liters of water a day.
He works eight hours a day.
The school year starts in September.
This is my school friend.
Never give up!
I'm not giving up on my dream.
The cost of living keeps rising.
I'll pay all the expenses.

tips: Mostly plural: трошкови пута (travel costs), трошкови живота (cost of living), трошкови смештаја (accommodation costs). Покрити трошкове means to cover the expenses.

examples.en: The children wear costumes for the masquerade.
I forgot my swimsuit.
He was in despair after being fired.
The food at the hotel was terrible.
This is an ancient city.
We are reading about the ancient Greeks.
I didn't expect this many people.
Why do you need so much time?
He stopped to catch his breath.
I was left breathless.
The village is located in the river valley.
It's spring, and the valley is full of flowers.
He fell asleep on the couch in front of the TV.
We bought a new couch.
He keeps checking his phone.
I'm checking whether the door is locked.
I have fond memories of my childhood.
Keep this in memory of me.
I like to walk along the river.
He walks the dog twice a day.

tips: In the sense of strolling it is reflexive: «шетам се поред реке».
A dog is walked without «се»: шетати пса (acc.). With «се» you walk yourself: шетам се по парку.

examples.en: Uncle Mile lives in Canada.
We're going to my uncle's for the weekend.
I didn't get a single cent.
It costs nine euros fifty cents.
The economic crisis hit everyone.
They are going through a crisis in their marriage.

examples.sr: Мој деда је био [офѝцӣр] у војсци.
examples.en: My grandfather was an officer in the army.
The officer gave an order.
Take this pill before bed.
He takes painkillers.
He doesn't care about fame.

examples.sr: У суботу нам је [сла̏ва], Свети Никола.
examples.en: On Saturday we have our slava, St. Nicholas.

note: slava is the feast day of a family's patron saint
tips: «Слава» is also the family feast on the day of the clan's patron saint, passed down the male line. Do not confuse it with plain «glory».
It is also the family's patron saint day: it lasts three days and guests come. Greet the host with «Срећна слава, домаћине!». Do not come empty-handed.
It is also the family feast on the patron saint's day: «славити славу», greeting «срећна слава!». It is held at the home of the eldest man.

examples.en: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
He succeeded in spite of everything.

examples.sr: Хтео сам да дођем, [међу̀тӣм] нисам стигао.
examples.en: I wanted to come, however, I didn't make it.
However, things are not that simple.

tips: Међутим usually comes after the first words of the sentence, set off by commas: «Мама је, међутим, само блефирала».

examples.en: I felt awkward asking.
It smells unpleasant in the basement.
On Sundays he plays golf with his boss.
The golf course is near the hotel.
I'm still in shock.

examples.sr: То је за мене био прави [шо̏к].
examples.en: That was a real shock for me.
I haven't had a drop of alcohol.
Put three drops in each eye.

note: feminine despite the consonant ending: ова кап, gen. капи

examples.en: You can pick up the key at the hotel reception.
The embassy is holding a reception for guests.
Put on a hat, it's cold outside.
In summer he always wears a cap with a visor.
I have a piece of good news!
In the morning I read the news on my phone.
I took a tablet for a headache.
These tablets are sold without a prescription.
Tomorrow I'm having a blood test.

examples.sr: Детаљна [анали́за] података трајала је недељу дана.
examples.en: The detailed analysis of the data took a week.
We got up at dawn.
They talked until dawn.

examples.sr: Испоставило се да је био страни [шпѝјӯн].
examples.en: It turned out he was a foreign spy.
I like spy movies.
The children throw stones into the river.
The road is full of stones.
His grandfather was Jewish.
Jews once lived in Dorćol.
Last night we watched a war movie.
Grandpa often tells war stories.

note: «ратни» relates to war; «војни» to the army

examples.en: She studies at the university in Belgrade.
Our university has ten faculties.
I study in the library until closing.
I borrowed a book from the library.
Thank you in advance!
You have to buy the tickets in advance.
I lost one glove.
Put on gloves, it's below zero outside.

tips: Mostly plural «рукавице» for a pair of gloves or mittens; singular «рукавица» is one glove.

examples.en: The truck is carrying a heavy load.
I don't want to be a burden to you.
Serbia was once a kingdom.
They lived in a faraway kingdom.
They found a hidden camera in the room.
He has a hidden talent for singing.
This is a very useful app.
Thanks for the useful advice.

tips: It means «beneficial, handy». Healthy food is not «корисна храна» but «здрава храна»; «корисне бактерије» are beneficial bacteria.

examples.en: The robot vacuums the floor for us.
I'm not a robot, I need a rest!
We spend the summer at Grandma's in the village.
Some old woman was sitting on the bench.
What's the date today?
Enter your date of birth.
He is allegedly very rich.
Supposedly, they're getting married in May.
I never pictured you like that.

examples.sr: Затворим очи и [замѝшљам] да лежим на плажи.
examples.en: I close my eyes and imagine I'm lying on the beach.
The Church of Saint Sava is in Vračar.
We visited an old Greek temple.
The police will question all the witnesses.
We have to examine all the possibilities.
Prices rose by ten percent.
I'm one hundred percent sure.
He didn't mention that he has a wife.

examples.sr: Као што сам већ [помѐнуо], сутра не радимо.
examples.en: As I already mentioned, we're not working tomorrow.
I suggested going to the seaside.
What would you offer us for dinner?

examples.sr: Стари [ло̏рд] живео је у великом дворцу.
examples.en: The old lord lived in a large castle.
He acts like some kind of lord.
The police are searching for the missing boy.
He has been searching for his father for years.
I like dark chocolate.
Let's have some hot chocolate.
The wolf killed all the sheep.
The lawyer refuted all the evidence.
The helicopter landed on the hospital roof.
The injured man was flown out by helicopter.
Christmas is my favorite holiday.
Happy holidays!

examples.sr: Нови телефон стиже на [тр̏жӣште] у мају.
examples.en: The new phone comes to market in May.
The real estate market is falling.

examples.sr: Не волим да причам о [полѝтичким] темама.
examples.en: I don't like to talk about political topics.
The country is in a political crisis.
Our parents gave us their blessing.
This child is a real blessing.
I need to do the laundry.
The washing machine broke down.
Everything is covered in dust.
Wipe the dust off the shelves.
Our neighbor has a big dog.
We invited the neighbors to lunch.

note: masculine, but declines like a feminine noun: комшију, комшије
tips: The female neighbor is комшиница: «Рекла ми је комшиница...». The word is from Turkish and very common in Serbia.
A Turkish loanword, but a perfectly neutral everyday word. Like сапун (soap) and сат (hour, clock), it is ordinary vocabulary, not archaic.

examples.en: Tomorrow I'm working the night shift.
The change of government brought big changes.
He gave her a bouquet of roses.
This rose smells wonderful.
Excuse me, where is the restroom?
I urgently need to go to the toilet.

forms: наиђем, наиђу; past наишао; impf. наилазити

examples.en: I came across an interesting article.
If you run into a problem, call me.

tips: It means to meet or find something by chance: «наићи на + acc.»; impf. наилазити. For a planned meeting use састати се, and the general word is срести (се).

examples.en: Admission to the concert is free.
This is a free app.
Don't be such a loser!
The loser pays for the drinks.
The ball broke the window glass.
Careful, there's broken glass on the floor!
This is private property.
We entered enemy territory.
Smoking destroys the lungs.
Breathe in the fresh air with full lungs.
After much thought, he agreed.
I like your way of thinking.
What make is your car?
Grandpa collects postage stamps.
I was sick, therefore I didn't come.
It's raining, so we're staying home.

note: bookish; in speech «зато» is more common

examples.en: I filed a complaint with the building management.
The company's management made a decision.
The ice on the lake isn't solid yet.
He has firm views.

examples.sr: Пао је на [тло̏] и није се померао.
examples.en: He fell to the ground and didn't move.
This soil is suitable for grapes.

examples.sr: Пала ми је на памет једна [ми̑сао].
examples.en: A thought came to my mind.
He was deep in thought.

note: feminine despite the ending: та мисао, gen. мисли

examples.en: Somebody pushed me into the water.
Push the door, it's open.
I was born in May.
The first of May is Labor Day.
Put on a coat, it's cold.
She bought a new winter coat.

note: means a coat, nothing to do with "kaput"

examples.en: Pack clean underwear and socks.
He opened the door in his underpants.
The police have not yet established his identity.
For years he hid his true identity.
The rocket flew toward the Moon.
I forgot my tennis racket.
Give me your phone number.
I'm waiting for an important phone call.
During the week I rarely go out.
You rarely see something like that.
I had a happy childhood.
We've known each other since childhood.
Who will you vote for?
I didn't vote in the last election.
The suspect signed a confession.
She received a lifetime achievement award.
Your daughter is a real beauty.
Children love the fairy tale of Sleeping Beauty.
She has a very strong personality.
He is a well-known public figure.
I love the sea, especially in June.
Don't go there, especially not alone.
She works at the Ministry of Education.
The ministry announced new measures.
Don't cry, Mommy is here.
Come to Mommy, son.
The elevator isn't working again.
I'm taking the elevator to the fifth floor.
We've been living together for five years.
Let's have lunch together.

note: colloquial; not the same as «скупа» (expensive, f.)

examples.en: Let's celebrate your success!
This movie made him famous.
The dog is happily wagging its tail.
My brother only listens to rap.
Tomorrow I have a job interview.
He gave an interview to a newspaper.
There are no free spaces in the parking lot.
Parking in the city center is expensive.
I'm interested in Serbian culture.
That's a matter of general knowledge.
The commander ordered a retreat.
Report to the commander immediately.
I need an assistant in the shop.
He is the deputy director.

examples.sr: Мој прадеда је био [бо́рац] у Другом светском рату.
examples.en: My great-grandfather was a soldier in World War II.
Don't worry, she's a real fighter.
Don't move!
I'll help you move the furniture.
This mattress is too soft.
He has a soft heart.
Tomorrow I have a lecture at nine.
I wasn't at the lecture yesterday.
We planted tomato seeds.
Buy some flower seeds.
By the way, where did you buy that jacket?
He only said it in passing.
He grabbed me by the arm.
Grab the bag and run!
The prime minister held a press conference.
He met with the Prime Minister of Serbia.
Grandma says a prayer before meals.
You are the answer to my prayers.

meanings: auntie (a child's word for an adult woman)

examples.en: Aunt Mira is coming to visit us.

examples.sr: Слушај шта ти каже [те̏та] у вртићу.
examples.en: Listen to what the teacher at kindergarten tells you.

note: colloquial; children call any adult woman this

examples.en: She likes romance movies.
He wrote her a love letter.
Can you lend me a pencil?
Write the test in pencil, not in ballpoint pen.

note: primarily a pencil; a ballpoint pen is «хемијска (оловка)»
tips: «Хемијска оловка» or just «хемијска» is a ballpoint pen. But adults often call a pen «оловка» too: «Имате ли оловку?» may mean a pen.
In everyday speech «оловка» is both a pencil and a pen; strictly a pen is «хемијска оловка». If a Serb asks «имаш ли оловку?», they most likely need a pen.

examples.en: All the evidence points to him.
He keeps pointing out my mistakes.
Don't stand on the edge of the cliff.
She was on the verge of tears.
Just act naturally.
Of course I'll come!
We had a very pleasant evening.
Her husband is a nice man.

note: «пријатно!» is also said to mean «enjoy your meal»

examples.en: Thank you for your presence.
Don't say that in front of the children.
We visited the Resava Cave.
It's dark and cold in the cave.
He speaks with a British accent.
The British government made a decision.
I called a repairman to fix the faucet.
He is a real master of the barbecue.

tips: «Мајсторе!» is a form of address to a repairman, a taxi driver, a driver, and jokingly to anyone who did something cool: «Ти си цар!».

examples.en: This is my husband Petar.
She came to the celebration with her husband.
Bring all the necessary documents.
Sign this document.
A collision happened at the intersection.
Nobody was hurt in the crash.
What's the use of that?
He acts only in his own interest.

tips: Корист is use or benefit: нема користи од тога means there is no use in it.

examples.en: I saw hatred in his eyes.
There is no hatred between them.
The match is broadcast live.
I've never seen them in person.
Let's talk frankly.
He openly admitted that he was wrong.
Grandpa built this house by himself.
We want to build a better future.
What was the motive for the crime?

examples.sr: Цвеће је чест [мо̀тӣв] на његовим сликама.
examples.en: Flowers are a frequent motif in his paintings.
I felt great sadness.
They say he died of grief.
The police made the arrest at dawn.
After his arrest he was released on bail.
He has trouble showing emotions.
It was a day full of emotions.
I was almost hit by a car.
I almost forgot your birthday.
He made a good impression on everyone.
What is your first impression?

tips: «Оставити утисак» means to make an impression, «стећи утисак да...» to get the impression that.... Another sense is an imprint.

examples.en: The couch is covered in cat hair.

examples.sr: Није му фалила ни [дла̏ка] с главе.
examples.en: Not a hair on his head was harmed.

tips: Длака is body hair and animal fur: мачја длака, длака у јелу (a hair in the food). «Без длаке на језику» means to speak bluntly.
Длака is body or facial hair and animal fur; hair on the head is «коса». Hence the idioms нема длаке на језику and висити о длаци (to hang by a thread).

examples.en: I haven't been to Paris so far.
Where have you been until now?
The king lived in this palace.
The trial is at the Palace of Justice.
Children get in for free.
Nothing in life is free.
Preparing for the exam takes a month.
All the preparations for the celebration are done.
The store is open until nine.
He is a very open person.
I'll make a tomato salad.
She ordered chicken with a salad.

tips: Салата is both a salad dish («шопска салата», «салата од цвекле») and lettuce, which is «зелена салата».

examples.en: He gave her a gold necklace.
The dog has a red collar.
The pilot sits in the cockpit.
Where is the fitting room?
The children are screaming in the yard.
Stop screaming!
Our team plays in the first league.

examples.sr: Заборави је, није она у твојој [ли̑ги].
examples.en: Forget her, she's out of your league.
He scored a goal in the last minute.
This gift is a real hit!

related.en: to hit the mark, to guess

examples.en: The knight carried a sword and a shield.
He used the hostage as a human shield.
Drink a large amount of water.
The amount of work is huge.
Do you need a bag?
She put the bread in a bag.

tips: «Кеса не треба» (I don't need a bag) is the stock phrase at the checkout.

examples.sr: О томе смо причали на [прѐтходном] састанку.
examples.en: We talked about it at the previous meeting.
The previous tenant left a mess.
The bread is still fresh.
Go out for some fresh air.
What sport do you do?
Football is the most popular sport in Serbia.
He is an honest and hardworking man.

examples.sr: Да будем [по̀штен], ни мени се не свиђа.
examples.en: To be honest, I don't like it either.
Someone's phone was left on the table.
I heard someone's footsteps.
See you in two weeks.
He hit seven numbers in the lottery.
In my rush I forgot my wallet.
There's no rush, we have plenty of time.
The court will deliver the verdict tomorrow.
The lawyer will appeal the ruling.

tips: Common phrases: донети пресуду (to pass judgment), жалити се на пресуду (to appeal a verdict), ослобађајућа пресуда (an acquittal).

examples.en: I want to talk to the manager.
He works as a sales manager.
Three men walked into the bank.
I saw three men running away.

note: only for men; for a mixed group use «троје»

examples.en: The dog jumped over the fence.
Hold on to the railing on the stairs.
He is the world tennis champion.
Bravo, you're my champion!
This is homemade plum rakija.
Did you do your homework?

tips: At school «домаћи» on its own means homework: Урадио сам домаћи. In full: домаћи задатак.
«Домаћи» alone is homework: in full «домаћи задатак» or «домаћи рад», but in speech the second word is dropped.
In speech домаћи means homework: домаћи (задатак). The same shorthand is used for купаћи, возачка, чланска, даљински, пешачки.

examples.en: These are the basic rules of the game.
We went to elementary school together.

note: основна школа is school for grades 1 to 8

examples.en: Smoking is a bad habit.
Out of habit I get up at six.

tips: «По навици» means out of habit: «Још спавам по навици у твојој мајици».
